rows: Record Q1 - total revenue $133.4M (+167%), the 14th consecutive quarter of sequential growth and 28% above Q4 2021.
Domestic revenue +214% on triple-digit growth across traditional channels, world-class retailer expansion, and rapid scaling of club and vending.
DSD distributor revenues surged 395%; the national distribution network reached ~99% of the US population.
Principal headwind: gross margin compression to 40.4% (from 41.1%) - higher-cost imported international cans, raw material inflation, and dilutive club-channel mix (secondary repack facilities).
Management implemented a frontline price increase effective April 1, but declined to disclose its magnitude ('sufficient amount').
High-cost international cans expected to peak in Q2 (further pressuring margins) and be cycled through by end of Q3, with gross margins recovering toward the mid-40s by Q4 and into 2023.
April 1 price increase will not be visible in scanner data until ~Q3, continuing into Q4.
New CFO transition: Jarrod Langhans replaced retiring Edwin Negron (announced April 18).
A previously disclosed SEC inquiry remains ongoing with no material update; FY2021 10-K internal control weaknesses expected to be remediated by year-end.
Club channel contributed $26M+ in Q1 (Sam's Club nationwide rollout added 589 locations, more than doubling the club store count); Costco Q1 revenue up over 1,100%.
Convenience the next frontier (70% of energy drinks sold there); convenience locations up 88% to ~64,000; long runway in door count and offerings.
G&A leveraged to 9% of sales (from 16%) on strong revenue growth; net income $6.7M ($0.09 EPS) up from $0.6M ($0.01).
Europe/Nordics down ~18% on FX translation, timing of trade campaigns/flavor launches, and supply chain delays; full-year international growth target reiterated at 10-15%.
Celsius is incremental to the category - contributed ~38% of category growth, mostly new-to-category consumers with only slight cannibalization; 50/50 male-female demographic.
Summer flavor launches: Strawberry Lemonade and Arctic Vibe; HEAT on-the-go sticks launched at Walmart and nationwide.
Any signs of consumer weakness from distributors or sales teams in any geography; how is the company thinking about pricing given Monster's price action and the likely category follow?

Acknowledged broad concern over recession and non-transitory inflation; consumer sentiment is mixed. Confirmed a frontline price increase with notices issued April 1, taking effect over the coming couple of quarters; Celsius can hold a premium position given favorable pricing-elasticity testing. The increase offsets inflationary costs and gives leeway on future promotional adjustments.
Price Increase Scope & CFO Early Observations
Was the April 1 price increase across the entire portfolio and what was the amount; CFO's early observations on opportunities (return optimization, SKU management, profitability, working capital)?

Declined to disclose the percentage of the price increase, saying only it has been implemented within the frontline pricing portfolio and is a 'sufficient amount' to protect against inflation. CFO described 'blocking and tackling' - focusing on people, processes and technology in finance, building data-analytics capability and a G&A team to support growth.
Does Celsius deliver DSD to club stores, and how does club-channel velocity compare to other channels?

Club channel growth has been surprising; Costco an extreme success (told it is one of the top-selling beverages in Costco's energy set). The club business is mainly direct with some DSD; the big opportunity ahead is further leveraging Sam's Club and BJ's. Club growth did not cannibalize other channels.
Why did freight expense rise only modestly ($3.2M to $4.2M) despite strong growth; is there any timing distortion in club stores (inventory fill) affecting future comps?

CFO attributed favorable freight to good management, mix (Costco), packaging differences, and the orbit model enabling lower-cost local freight - though it will vary by volume, packaging and growth location. CEO: Costco revenue is now standard recurring revenue; the Sam's Club quarter included both a fill-in and a reorder, with a better run-rate read after Q2.
More detail on the BJ's club opportunity and next steps; management's overall take on spring resets.

Celsius is in some BJ's stores, testing regionally, and is confident of a larger rollout/reset within the year (specific revenue premature); exploring additional pack sizes to improve club margins. On spring resets, cited the key accounts team, the Circle K rollout (6,000 locations, 13 divisions, some delayed by labor shortages), Walmart/Target expansion, and successful new flavors.

Launch cadence for the balance of the year (Strawberry Lemonade, Arctic Vibe, ~38 SKUs); anything on on-the-go sticks; international territories outside Nordics/China that could be million-plus this year?

Highlighted Strawberry Lemonade (summer launch) and Arctic Vibe (frozen berry flavor expanding the vibe portfolio in convenience), about three flavors arriving over coming months. On-the-go sticks (including new HEAT sticks at Walmart and nationwide) have growing demand but remain a smaller revenue portion. Declined to name specific international territories as premature, but cited strong Tier-1 distributor interest.
Pricing Lag in Scanner Data & Category Incrementality

Why does scanner data since April 1 show no price increase - is there a lag, does reduced promotion offset it, was there March selling-in ahead of the increase; how incremental is Celsius (new consumers vs share from Monster/Red Bull)?

The frontline price increase will not be visible in scanner data until ~Q3 (retailers require notice, issued April 1), continuing into Q4; promotions had been reduced. On incrementality, Celsius is not cannibalizing leading players, contributed ~38% of category growth, has a 50:50 male-female demographic, and brings mostly new-to-category consumers with only slight cannibalization.
Convenience Channel Growth Source & Gross Margin Initiatives
Jeremy Pearlman, Maxim Group (for Anthony Vendetti)
Where will convenience-channel growth come from (within current stores or new store expansion); is there more room in the gross-margin-improvement initiatives or is it already baked in?

Celsius is 'backdooring' the energy category - strong on Amazon, club, grocery and mass - and convenience (70% of energy drinks sold there) is the next frontier with a long runway. On margins, Q1 had a meaningful international can mix, Q2 will see the percentage increase (further pressuring margins), and cans should be used up by end of Q3, returning gross margins to the mid-40s by Q4 and into 2023.
International Revenue Outlook & Inventory & Competitor Pricing
Should European revenues turn positive year-over-year or continue facing pressure; outlook for inventory-to-sales; could the Monster price increase prompt customers to load up on competitor product?

Reiterated a 10-15% full-year international revenue growth target despite Q1 timing-related delays, supply chain shortages and European logistical disruption. CFO: inventory reduced by ~$6M, with ~$20M of international cans on the books moving from deposit into inventory to be cycled through; current levels support a 97% fill rate. On competitor pricing, any price increase produces some load-ins, but management is confident Celsius's trajectory and distributor relationships will not slow.
